question.text: For companies with post-issue capital between Rs. 4,000 crore and Rs. 1 lakh crore, the minimum offer to public in an IPO must be at least __________ of the post-issue capital.

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI's minimum public offer thresholds are tiered based on post-issue capital. For companies with post-issue capital between Rs. 4,000 crore and Rs. 1 lakh crore, the minimum offer to the public must be at least 10% of the post-issue capital. The Trap: 25% is the default threshold for smaller companies (post-issue capital up to Rs. 1,600 crore) and is the most commonly remembered figure. The 15% and 20% options do not correspond to any actual SEBI threshold. Note: Remember the tiered structure: up to Rs. 1,600 crore = 25%; Rs. 1,600-4,000 crore = Rs. 400 crore worth; Rs. 4,000 crore to Rs. 1 lakh crore = 10%.
